speaker: Doctor
text:
Let's start with some basics: how long has your cough been persisting, and does it produce any phlegm? Also, have you noticed any fever or night sweats recently?

REQUEST TEST: Chest_XRay

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No acute infiltrates or consolidation. Mild bronchial wall thickening.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since the X-ray rules out pneumonia, have you been exposed to any chemicals, dust, or smoke lately, or do you have a history of allergies or asthma? Also, does your shortness of breath worsen with exercise or exertion?

REQUEST TEST: Spirometry

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: FEV1: 65% predicted, FVC: 80% predicted, FEV1/FVC Ratio: Decreased

speaker: Doctor
text:
That spirometry result indicates an obstructive pattern, which strongly suggests asthma or Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD). Have you smoked in the past or currently, and do you experience wheezing or a tightness in your chest? Additionally, has anyone in your family ever been diagnosed with asthma?

REQUEST TEST: Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Level

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Asthma. The combination of an obstructive spirometry pattern, normal Alpha-1 Antitrypsin levels (ruling out COPD due to protease deficiency), and the absence of acute infiltrates on X-ray points definitively to asthma.
